text:
Dallas keeps winning, and Sam Steel keeps waiting. The Stars have won eight of his last ten games; he has no points in any of them, and one goal and two assists through 18 games after 33 points in 73 games last season.

Our numbers split the blame. His team has scored 4.9 fewer goals than its chances deserved with him on the ice, which has cost him points, and that kind of luck usually swings back. But the chances have thinned too: over those ten games, Dallas generated 5.2 expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on against his usual 6.5, and at five on five the Stars take 48% of the expected goals with him out there, 4.8 points worse than without him.

He's still playing almost 16 minutes a night and killing penalties, the kind of player Evolving-Hockey valued at 1.1 wins last season. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking says 55% of his shots come off the rush, so he needs the puck moving the other way to be dangerous. The 131-point junior scorer from Regina has built an NHL career without big point totals. The drought is the part to watch.
